summary_paragraph: A woman with Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by gastrojejunal anastomotic ulcer and gastrostomy tube dependence was admitted for recurrent worsening epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the right upper quadrant with nausea/dry heaving and decreased oral intake. Evaluation showed stable vital signs and reassuring labs (normal WBC, lactate, lipase, and transaminases) with mild alkaline phosphatase elevation, and CT abdomen/pelvis demonstrated no abscess or acute intra-abdominal abnormality with the gastrostomy tube in unchanged position. She improved with IV hydration and an increased free-water flush regimen (to 100 mL every 4 hours), continued ulcer therapy (lansoprazole and sucralfate), antiemetics, and a multimodal pain plan including PRN oxycodone and initiation of gabapentin 300 mg three times daily, with plan for outpatient pain-clinic follow-up. She was discharged home ambulatory and stable, tolerating tube feeds and flushes, with return precautions and continuation of chronic medications including iron, statin, and psychiatric medications.
